metaData.title: What Justifies Zhipu's Trillion Valuation?
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the market logic behind Zhipu's trillion-HKD valuation: driven by scarcity, passive allocation, and narrative premium, while noting that roughly half of the valuation comes from real growth and the other half from structural amplification.
metaData.summary: Taking Zhipu's market cap surpassing one trillion HKD as a starting point, the article analyzes the company's 2025 financial report (revenue of 724 million yuan, net loss of 4.718 billion yuan, R&D expenditure of 3.18 billion yuan) and the technical performance of its GLM-5.2 model to explain why the market continues to push the stock price higher despite the clearly excessive valuation. The author identifies three underlying logics: a dual scarcity effect formed by the limited supply of Coding Plan on the product side and an extremely low free float (only about 2.67% of H-shares are tradable) on the capital side; concentrated passive buying triggered by inclusion in the Hang Seng Tech Index; and the scarcity narrative around foundational AI model companies. The article also references Keynes's beauty contest theory and Soros's reflexivity concept to analyze how prices become self-reinforcing. It warns of risks: the unlocking of restricted shares in July and slowing quarterly growth could lead to a valuation collapse, as well as potential competitive threats from DeepSeek and others. Finally, it points out that the risk-reward ratio at current prices is severely asymmetric, and whether Zhipu can transform its high valuation into an infrastructure platform position will be the key to long-term success.

mainPoints.point: The core driver of Zhipu's trillion valuation is not fundamentals, but scarcity.
mainPoints.explanation: Limited supply of Coding Plan on the product side, an extremely low free float on the capital side, coupled with passive allocation triggered by inclusion in the Hang Seng Tech Index, create a self-reinforcing cycle of excess demand.

mainPoints.point: A high valuation benefits Zhipu the company, but poses extreme risk to secondary investors.
mainPoints.explanation: High valuations provide financing and talent advantages, but with a PS ratio exceeding 1,200x, if quarterly growth slows from triple digits to double digits, the valuation could collapse in a correction.

mainPoints.point: The reflexivity theory explains how bubbles form and persist.
mainPoints.explanation: Market prices not only fail to reflect fundamentals, but can also change fundamentals by influencing financing, talent, and customer resources. As long as the cycle remains unbroken, calling it expensive cannot stop the price from rising.

mainPoints.point: The real risk Zhipu faces is the loss of its competitive advantage.
mainPoints.explanation: If competitors like DeepSeek release models with comparable performance that are more open, Zhipu's scarcity will disappear, and pricing power will shift accordingly.

keyQuotes: Everyone saw the numerical contrast. ... This article tries to explain another question: why is the price still rising when everyone thinks it's expensive?
No one is crazy. It's just that the rational behavior of all individuals combined has produced a seemingly crazy price.
In Soros's terms of 'reflexivity,' market prices do not merely reflect fundamentals; they may also change fundamentals in return.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.
